evals.prompt: PortQuay Conf is our community Go and Rust conference in Bristol - 320 people in the room, two tracks, one day, 14 March. The board voted last month to run it hybrid and that vote is settled, we are not reopening it. I have about 6,000 pounds left in the AV line and I need to know what to actually do for the remote side. Give me the plan.
evals.expected_output: A hybrid design that takes the format decision as closed, opens by establishing what the remote audience was promised, covers eligibility, parity depth, the cue track and remote-side staffing, hands equipment choices to the production scope, and is presented section by section for validation before the grid is published.
expectations: Does not re-argue whether the event should be hybrid and does not restate a cost or risk case against hybrid delivery
Does not recommend, name or compare any specific capture or encoding equipment such as cameras, encoders, capture cards, switchers, uplinks or return-audio hardware
Does not produce a streaming-platform comparison or recommend a specific streaming platform product
States that the eligible-session list and the required return path are handed to a separate production scope, which chooses the equipment
Asks what the remote audience was actually promised, and to whom, before recommending an eligibility rung
Asks how many of the rooms running at once can physically carry a feed
Records the promise as a single written sentence that every later choice is measured against
Covers all four of: which sessions the remote audience gets, how far a remote attendee's voice reaches the stage, the cue track the stream needs, and who staffs the remote side
Recommends one designated streamed room as the default eligibility rung, or justifies moving off it against the promise
Reports the staffing consequence for the budget, noting the feed itself survives a lean tier while the return path and the people watching it are cut first
Presents the plan section by section for validation rather than as one finished document
States that this must be settled before the session grid is published

evals.prompt: Two of us are running Datafold Days - one day, three tracks, about 250 people - and we have committed to a hybrid edition. My co-organizer thinks the cheapest remote programme is to just publish the recordings the following week and call that the remote track. If that is too thin, her fallback is to put a checkbox on the CFP form so each speaker can say they are happy to be streamed, and we stream whoever ticks it. She reckons that is cheaper than us hand-picking a remote line-up. Which of the two, and why?
evals.expected_output: A refusal of publish-the-recordings as a hybrid option at all, and a reasoned finding that a curated remote programme costs less than per-session speaker opt-in rather than more, with the two cost reasons and the coherence argument stated.
expectations: Rejects publishing the recordings afterwards as a remote programme rather than ranking it as the cheapest hybrid option
Names post-event publication as a different delivery mode - in-person with record and post - that this event has already decided against
Routes post-event publication of recordings to a separate content-repurposing scope
States that a curated remote programme costs less effort than per-session speaker opt-in, contradicting the premise in the prompt
Gives the reason that an opt-in can land in any room, so every room has to be instrumented
Gives the reason that constraining which rooms speakers may opt into stops it being an opt-in
States that curation and opt-in tie on how much of the programme a remote attendee can watch, because neither delivers a predictable share
States that the curated programme beats opt-in on coherence because opt-in produces holes at times nobody can predict
Concludes that the curated remote programme is the better of the two options offered
Notes that speaker opt-in stays usable where the consent record is already per-speaker and opt-out is genuinely offered
States that if opt-in is used, the resulting holes must be made legible rather than presented as a programme
Does not claim that streaming every session in every room gives a remote attendee the most coherent day
Does not invent an attendance, engagement or satisfaction figure to justify either option

evals.prompt: We are doing hybrid for the first time at Kestrel Summit - two rooms streamed, 180 in the building. The plan for the remote side is: open a #remote-questions channel in our Discord, tell people to drop questions in there, and ask each room's AV volunteer to keep half an eye on it between their other jobs. Costs us nothing extra. Sanity-check this for me?
evals.expected_output: A rejection of both halves of the plan - the unread question channel and the room volunteer doubling as remote advocate - with feed only named as the correct fallback where no person can be named, and the conditions that make a written asynchronous path legitimate instead.
expectations: Rejects an open remote question channel with nobody reading it during the session, rather than suggesting improvements to it
States that such a channel is worse than giving the remote audience no return path at all
Explains that it invites a question inside the session and drops it inside the same session, in front of the person who asked
Notes that the unread channel still carries a conduct or moderation duty with no responder
Rejects the room's own lead or AV volunteer doubling as the remote advocate
Explains that the room role owns the room's clock and that both jobs come due at the same moment
States that where no person can be named for a session, the correct answer is feed only rather than an unattended channel
Specifies that feed only requires publishing one line in advance, where remote attendees already look, saying questions are not taken live
States that under feed only the speaker is deliberately not told the remote audience is watching
Requires the remote-side person to be identified by name per streamed session rather than by function
Distinguishes a legitimate asynchronous written return path from the rejected channel by its stated answerer, its stated deadline and the stated place the answer appears
Does not resolve the problem by recommending additional equipment

evals.prompt: Fabricoil Conf: three rooms, all three carrying a live stream, 400 people in the building. Beyond the AV contractor I can free up exactly two volunteers for the whole day to look after remote. My instinct is to put both of them in the two busiest rooms so remote questions actually get asked. Tell me how to deploy them.
evals.expected_output: A deployment that puts at least one person off the floor watching the outgoing feed, naming the crossing where the cheaper off-floor watcher catches feed failures better than an in-room advocate, with no invented staffing ratio.
expectations: Recommends that at least one of the two people sits off the floor, in no room, watching the outgoing feed as a remote attendee receives it
States that a person standing beside the stage is the last to notice the stream has died
States that the off-floor watcher costs less than an in-room advocate and catches feed failures better
Identifies service inside a session - relaying a question, acknowledging remote, telling the speaker remote is there - as the only axis on which the in-room advocate beats the off-floor watcher
Notes that one watcher covers however many rooms exist while advocates scale with the number of streamed rooms
Notes that an advocate needs a session-by-session briefing on the programme while a watcher needs only the output
States that nobody standing in one room can see another room's output, given three rooms carry feeds
Does not invent a ratio of remote-side staff to remote attendees
Does not invent a ratio of remote-side staff to in-room staff
Assigns the remote side by name per streamed session rather than by function
States that any session left without a named remote-side person has its return path closed explicitly
Does not recommend the room lead or an AV crew member absorb the remote role as a third pair of hands

evals.prompt: Our run of show for Larkspur Dev Day is already written - minute by minute, MC lines, room leads, escalation path, the lot. Now I need the equivalent for the stream. Draft the stream's rundown for a day running 09:00 to 17:30 with one streamed room.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to author a second document, replaced by a specification of one added column on the existing run of show rows, with the synchronization rule, the three things each stream entry carries, gap rows, flagged spoken-announcement rows, and the handoff to the run-of-show scope.
expectations: Adds a column to the existing run of show rather than authoring a second, parallel document
Explains that two documents drift and that the drift is invisible until the day
States the synchronization rule that the room's transition and the stream's transition are the same row
Specifies that each row's stream entry says what the stream is showing at that moment - the stage, the slides, or a holding card
Specifies that each row's stream entry names who owns that decision, as a person rather than a function
Specifies that each row's stream entry says what the remote audience is being told
Keeps equipment detail out of the stream column
Gives every gap between sessions its own row with an entry in the stream column
Explains that a remote attendee cannot distinguish a scheduled break from a dead feed
Recommends a holding card naming what is happening and when the next session starts as the cheapest fix for a gap
Flags rows where the room is told something out loud that was never typed anywhere, such as a room change, a delay or a swapped speaker
Identifies rows that exist in only one column as the ones to re-read at the briefing
Hands the column to the run-of-show scope as an addition to its existing artifact

evals.prompt: Here is the disruption order our schedule owner handed down for Nimbus Conf: protect the plenary or keynote first, protect the headline commitment the audience showed up for next, minimize how many other sessions the fix disturbs, then lock the revised grid for the rest of the block. We are hybrid this year with two streamed rooms. Is that order good enough to run the day on?
evals.expected_output: A finding that the inherited order addresses a single audience while a hybrid has two, the three documented defaults that do exist, the two questions that have no documented answer, and a requirement to decide those two in writing in advance with the decider named.
expectations: Identifies that the inherited order names a single audience while a hybrid event has two
Answers that the order is not sufficient as written
States the documented default that the room keeps going and a dead feed is fixed in parallel, rather than pausing on reflex
States the documented default that the authority to give up on a feed sits inside the technical chain, escalated to a senior organizer
States that this call is never left with a volunteer alone
States the documented default that the remote side gets a named live-chat contact rather than an intermittently checked inbox
Names the contested-technician question - who wins when the remote-side person and the room lead need the same technician at once - as having no documented answer
Names whether a session moved to fix an in-room problem takes the remote programme with it as having no documented answer
Requires both open questions to be decided in advance and written into the day-of document
Requires recording who decided them
States that neither may be presented as inherited or standard practice
Does not fabricate an industry-standard rule for either open question

evals.prompt: Our title sponsor for Harborlight wants numbers on the remote side before they sign. They are asking what share of Q&A time remote will get, how many moderators we will run per hundred remote viewers, what stream latency we will hold to, and what remote attendance we should forecast against 500 in-person. Give me figures I can put in the deck.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to supply any of the four invented figures, replaced by the three completeness gates checkable before the first session and a short set of explicitly self-set metrics.
expectations: Declines to state a share of Q&A owed to the remote audience as a standard
Declines to state a remote-to-in-room or per-viewer staffing ratio
Declines to state a tolerable or target stream latency
Declines to forecast remote attendance from a published benchmark or a ratio to in-person headcount
States that academic conferencing turnout data transfers poorly to technology events
Offers instead the gate that every remote-eligible session has a named person on the remote side, or its return path is explicitly closed
Offers the gate that every cue row changing what the room sees also says what the stream shows
Offers the gate that the disruption priority order states in writing what happens when a remote-side failure and an in-room failure compete
Proposes remote questions that reached a stage against remote questions asked, labelled as a self-set metric
Proposes announcements made in the room that never reached the remote channel, labelled as a self-set metric
Labels every proposed metric as one this event sets rather than an industry standard
Recommends recording the chosen metrics, and the change each would trigger, before the event rather than after

evals.prompt: Every speaker at Tessellate signed our standard recording-and-publication release when they were accepted - same form we have used for four years. This year we are streaming two rooms live, including the Q&A at the end of each talk. Anything I need to do on the consent side, or are we covered?
evals.expected_output: A finding that the existing release does not settle a live feed, with the specific questions a live feed adds about in-room questioners, signage, the boundary of the session and same-day withdrawal, settled before the eligibility column is marked.
expectations: Answers that the existing recording release does not settle it
States that consent for a recording and consent for a live feed are different permissions
Raises whether in-room questioners' voices and faces go out on the outgoing live feed
Requires a decision on whether audience questions are on camera, off camera, or audio only
Requires a visible sign in the room telling attendees the session is going out live, placed where they see it before they speak
Requires a decision on where the feed cuts at the end of a session - at the last word, or carrying the room emptying
Raises what happens if a speaker withdraws consent on the day, and who holds the authority to cut the feed
States that the same-day withdrawal question has no standard answer and must be decided in advance with a named person holding the authority
States that a live feed publishes before anyone can check it, so none of this can be settled in an edit
States that a speaker's opt-out has to be honoured in the room rather than in an edit
Requires the consent question settled before the eligibility column is marked, not after
Routes the consent record itself to the speaker-experience scope rather than building a second record

evals.prompt: Rhizome Conf sold 140 virtual tickets at 45 euros each this year, and the listing said live Q&A with every speaker. Last year's remote crowd told us they felt like they were watching TV. I want to reserve 25% of every Q&A for remote questions and tell the moderators to eyeball it. Does that work?
evals.expected_output: A replacement of the proportional rule with a sequence rule and the reason it survives a cut-short Q&A, the paid promise treated as the thing the parity rung is measured against, and the full four-step relay mechanic including the post-answer confirmation.
expectations: Rejects a proportional share of Q&A as the rule and recommends a sequence rule instead
Gives a concrete sequence rule, such as remote taking the first question of every Q&A, or room and remote alternating until time runs out
Explains that a proportion has to be computed under time pressure by someone counting hands
Explains that a proportion fails silently when Q&A is cut short while a sequence rule survives being cut short
Treats the promise sold - live Q&A with every speaker - as what the parity rung is measured against
Notes that a paid virtual ticket sold on participation promotes the parity rung above the default
Requires the relay person to tell the speaker before the session that remote is watching and that questions will arrive through them
Requires the relay person to select from the remote channel rather than read aloud everything typed
Requires the relay person to name who is asking and where they are from before reading the question
Requires the relay person to confirm in the channel afterwards that the question was asked
Puts the reserved-time rule on the cue sheet row rather than only in a briefing document
Does not settle for feed only or for a written-answers-later path given the promise sold
Does not invent a figure for how much Q&A time the remote audience should receive

evals.prompt: The grid for Vellum Days went public on Monday - four tracks, 31 sessions. Marketing has now decided we are doing hybrid. Two speakers have since said they do not want to be streamed, and the whole Thursday workshop block is hands-on and dense, so live Q&A was never really the shape of those. I was going to publish a separate remote agenda page on the site so it stays clean. Where do I start?
evals.expected_output: An eligibility column added to the already-published grid rather than a separate agenda page, the publication-retraction problem named, the column's three fields including the explicit closed entry, and an asynchronous written return path with its three stated commitments for the workshop block.
expectations: Marks eligibility as a column on the already-published grid rather than as a separate remote agenda or second page
Explains that a second document has a second update path and that the missed update is always on the document fewer people open
States that removing a session from the remote programme after the grid is public is a retraction rather than a decision
Requires consent and instrumentation settled before the grid is marked
Specifies that the column holds eligible or not eligible as a binary, not a plan
Specifies that the column holds the return path for that session where it differs from the event default
Specifies that the column holds the named remote-side person for that session, or an explicit closed where nobody is available
Explains that an explicit closed separates a deliberate decision from a row nobody has looked at
Recommends an asynchronous written return path for the dense workshop block rather than live relay
Requires that path to state who answers, by when, and where the answer appears
States that without those three commitments the asynchronous path is the rejected unread channel wearing a promise
Does not move or re-place any session on the published grid
Presents the plan in the order promise, eligibility, parity, staffing, cue track
